sourcesAndMethod: Étienne Brunet / Eduscol-derived French frequency list. Parsed programmatically, normalized, deduplicated by surface form, and ordered by descending frequency.
Used to cross-check the classic frequency backbone against a modern learner-oriented spoken-frequency list and identify a small set of higher-utility beginner words.
Used only as a multilingual sense spot-check where concept-linked French, English, and Persian entries were available. Ambiguous automatic matches were not accepted blindly.

The main sheet is frequency-first and beginner-curated. It contains exactly 1,000 unique French entries. Row order is the rank. English and Persian cells give concise primary learner meanings, not exhaustive dictionary definitions.

A small number of dated, literary, inflected, or low-utility entries in the lower-frequency portion were replaced with practical beginner vocabulary such as greetings, close family, travel, food, study, and modern technology terms.
